source_policy.technical_claims: Prefer official standards, specifications, documentation, and first-party engineering reports.
source_policy.role_claims: Employer materials establish observed employer practice, not a universal definition.
source_policy.case_claims: Vendor and employer outcomes remain attributed and are not treated as independently verified.
source_policy.volatile_sources: Record an access date and restate durable concepts independently of a current interface or product name.

sources.title: Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE), Seattle
claim_uses: Observed FDE lifecycle from discovery through rollout and adoption
Security and governance collaboration
Measurable workflow outcomes
sources.limitations: One employer's current role design; not a universal competency standard.

sources.title: Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE), San Francisco
claim_uses: Field patterns, playbooks, building blocks, and product feedback
sources.limitations: Employer-authored and vacancy-specific.

sources.title: Forward Deployed Software Engineer
claim_uses: Customer-embedded software engineering as an observed FDSE pattern
sources.limitations: Supports a narrower employer-specific FDSE title; vacancy may disappear.

sources.title: OpenAI launches the Deployment Company
claim_uses: Workflow diagnosis, prioritization, design, testing, deployment, and measurable results as a current deployment model
sources.limitations: Company positioning; not independent evidence of results.

sources.title: Introducing OpenAI Presence
claim_uses: Least-required access, policy, approval and escalation
Deployment simulation and production feedback
Generalizing field learning
sources.limitations: Vendor product description and early deployment claims.

sources.title: Understand users and their needs
claim_uses: Understand the whole problem and context before selecting a solution
sources.limitations: Government service context; transfer to commercial deployments requires judgment.

sources.title: Start by learning user needs
claim_uses: Interview and observe real users
Treat stakeholder opinions as assumptions until evidenced
sources.limitations: Guidance, not comparative proof of one research method.

sources.title: Map a user's whole problem
claim_uses: Whole-journey mapping and broken handoffs
sources.limitations: Does not prescribe a single mapping notation.

sources.title: What a service is
claim_uses: A service delivers an outcome across paths, not only a digital interface
sources.limitations: Public-service framing; book generalizes cautiously.

sources.title: Introduction to designing government services
claim_uses: End-to-end, front-to-back, cross-channel, secure-by-design service thinking
sources.limitations: High-governance environment; not a universal delivery process.

sources.title: Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN), Version 2.0.2
claim_uses: A standardized notation exists for process modeling
sources.limitations: The book does not require BPMN; notation choice depends on audience and purpose.

sources.title: Using data to improve your service
claim_uses: Define outcome, use, and adoption measures early and segment them
sources.limitations: Examples are public-service oriented.

sources.title: Measuring service benefits
claim_uses: Baseline benefits and monitor evidence to continue, change, or stop
sources.limitations: Guidance does not establish causal attribution by itself.

sources.title: Set up and manage user support
claim_uses: Support demand, service levels, and feedback loops are part of service operation
sources.limitations: Specific support channels vary by organization.

sources.title: Measuring user satisfaction
claim_uses: Continuous feedback, dropout evidence, and satisfaction as one signal
sources.limitations: Satisfaction alone is not proof of workflow value.

sources.title: The C4 model for visualising software architecture
claim_uses: Hierarchical context and container abstractions; notation and tooling independence
sources.limitations: C4 does not by itself express responsibility, trust, or failure semantics.

sources.title: AWS Well-Architected Framework
claim_uses: Operational excellence, security, reliability, performance, cost, sustainability, and explicit tradeoffs
sources.limitations: Cloud-provider guidance; extract provider-neutral principles.

sources.title: What is the Azure Well-Architected Framework?
claim_uses: Reliability, security, cost, operational excellence, and performance tradeoffs
sources.limitations: Cloud-provider guidance; not proof of implementation quality.

sources.title: Architecture design principles
claim_uses: Self-healing, redundancy, operations, identity, and failure-mode analysis
sources.limitations: Provider examples must not become mandatory architecture.

sources.title: OpenAPI Specification 3.2.0
claim_uses: Machine-readable HTTP API interface descriptions
sources.limitations: An interface description does not guarantee correct semantics, compatibility, or operations.

sources.title: AsyncAPI Specification 3.0.0
claim_uses: Protocol-agnostic descriptions for message-driven interfaces
sources.limitations: Does not replace domain semantics, delivery guarantees, or operational design.

sources.title: JSON Schema Draft 2020-12
claim_uses: Schema vocabulary for structural validation
sources.limitations: Structural validity is not semantic or business validity.

sources.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
claim_uses: HTTP method semantics and idempotency definitions
sources.limitations: Application-level retry safety still depends on operation semantics and implementation.

sources.title: Making retries safe with idempotent APIs
claim_uses: Client request identifiers, semantic equivalence, retry behavior, and complexity tradeoffs
sources.limitations: AWS practice report, not an independent comparative study.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 25012:2008 Data quality model
claim_uses: General model for structured-data quality requirements and evaluation
sources.limitations: Full standard text is not reproduced; operational rules must be contextualized.

sources.title: Zero Trust Architecture
claim_uses: No implicit trust based only on network location; protect resources; authenticate and authorize
sources.limitations: Architectural guidance, not a product checklist or certification.

sources.title: Best Current Practice for OAuth 2.0 Security
claim_uses: Current OAuth 2.0 security best practices
sources.limitations: Only applicable where OAuth 2.0 is used; implementation remains context-specific.

sources.title: Semantic Versioning 2.0.0
claim_uses: Major, minor, and patch compatibility signaling for declared public APIs
sources.limitations: Requires a declared public API and does not solve deployment or data compatibility alone.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
claim_uses: Current status and lifecycle framing of AI risk management
sources.limitations: Framework revision is active; book must name the cited version.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
claim_uses: Voluntary, use-case-agnostic lifecycle risk-management framing
sources.limitations: Not a certification, law, or prescriptive implementation recipe.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile
claim_uses: Generative-AI risks organized around govern, map, measure, and manage
sources.limitations: Risk taxonomy and actions require tailoring to the workflow and authority context.

sources.title: Evals
claim_uses: Dataset-driven evaluation concepts and current platform lifecycle
sources.limitations: Specific Evals platform is scheduled for deprecation in late 2026; cite concepts, not durable UI/API promises.

sources.title: Agent evals
claim_uses: Evaluation of agent behavior and traces
sources.limitations: Vendor-specific tooling evolves quickly.

sources.title: Safety best practices
claim_uses: Layered safeguards, testing, monitoring, and human review as vendor guidance
sources.limitations: Not a substitute for system-specific risk assessment or formal approval.

sources.title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
claim_uses: Task, trial, grader, transcript, outcome, harness, and suite distinctions
Capability versus regression evaluation
sources.limitations: Employer engineering guidance, not a neutral standard.

sources.title: Building effective agents
claim_uses: Prefer simple composable workflows where sufficient; give agents ground truth, checkpoints, and stopping conditions
sources.limitations: Vendor practice; architecture choices remain workload-specific.

sources.title: Production ML systems
claim_uses: The model is one component inside a broader production system
sources.limitations: Educational simplification; examples center on ML rather than every AI workflow.

sources.title: Monitoring ML systems
claim_uses: Monitor data and model quality in production, not service availability alone
sources.limitations: Metric selection and thresholds remain workflow-specific.

sources.title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2026
claim_uses: Current community taxonomy and mitigation prompts for common LLM application risks
sources.limitations: Community guide, not a formal standard or complete threat model.

sources.title: Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
claim_uses: Risk governance and cybersecurity outcomes across organizations
sources.limitations: Outcome framework; does not prescribe a complete control implementation.

sources.title: Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) Version 1.1
claim_uses: Secure software practices integrated into the development lifecycle
sources.limitations: Version 1.2 was draft as of the research cutoff; the book cites final 1.1.

sources.title: NIST Privacy Framework Version 1.0
claim_uses: Risk- and outcome-based privacy management across technologies and jurisdictions
sources.limitations: Not legal advice and not a jurisdiction-specific compliance mapping.

sources.title: Application Security Verification Standard
claim_uses: Versioned application-security verification requirements
sources.limitations: Scoping and level selection require security ownership and system context.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 25010:2023 Systems and software Quality Requirements and Evaluation
claim_uses: Software product quality model for requirements, measurement, and acceptance
sources.limitations: The standard record supports scope/version; full copyrighted text is not reproduced.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
claim_uses: Testable web accessibility success criteria
sources.limitations: Conformance does not alone establish complete usability or accessibility for every context.

sources.title: Deployment simulation: Stress testing models in deployment-like contexts
claim_uses: Deployment-like simulation can expose limits missed by static evaluation
sources.limitations: Company research source; simulation still cannot reproduce all production tails.

sources.title: Service Level Objectives
claim_uses: User-relevant indicators and objectives linked to action and tradeoffs
sources.limitations: Practices must be adapted to service maturity and business context.

sources.title: Signals
claim_uses: Traces, metrics, and logs as distinct telemetry signals
sources.limitations: Instrumentation semantics and product support vary by version.

sources.title: Canarying Releases
claim_uses: Partial, time-limited rollout; control/canary comparison; absolute SLO checks
sources.limitations: Canary design is system-specific and preproduction cannot be assumed equivalent to production.

sources.title: Recommendations for safe deployment practices
claim_uses: Small quality-gated changes, progressive exposure, health checks, stop and recovery
sources.limitations: Provider guidance; mechanisms and thresholds depend on the deployment.

sources.title: Release Engineering
claim_uses: Automation, consistency, self-service, and release velocity
sources.limitations: Large-scale Google practice requires adaptation.

sources.title: Reliable Product Launches at Scale
claim_uses: Launch review, operability, ownership, and readiness questions
sources.limitations: Review process should scale to risk rather than imitate Google organization structure.

sources.title: Incident Response Recommendations and Considerations for Cybersecurity Risk Management
claim_uses: Integrate incident response across cybersecurity risk management
sources.limitations: Organizational process guidance, not an incident-command script for every event.

sources.title: Postmortem Culture: Learning from Failure
claim_uses: Blameless incident records connecting impact, causes, actions, and follow-up
sources.limitations: A postmortem practice must align with local safety, legal, and employment obligations.

sources.title: Prepare for cloud operations
claim_uses: Document operations, change, release, disaster recovery, and continuous improvement
sources.limitations: Azure framing; responsibilities must be translated to the actual operating model.
